why: The function is in the joint sign pattern, not in the low-rank head, so the top-8 directions act only as their 11.8 % energy share along the delta (like a ~0.12 dose), which lands on the plain dose curve about a third of the way from base 45 % to RL 93 %, not at RL level.
Top-8 directions carry only their 11.8 % projection on the coherent sign pattern, equivalent to a ~0.12 dose; on the near-linear plain dose curve (224 at a=0, 405 at a=0.25) that gives about 305/500.
A random rank-8 direction has about 1/leverage (~1/1000) of the RL direction's effect per unit energy, so the plain base stays at its ~45 % level.
Taking out the top 8 directions leaves 88 % of the delta's energy and almost all of its sign pattern, which is like a ~0.88 dose and so gives near-RL plain accuracy (~92 %).
24 late-MLP rank-3 terms hold a tiny share of the coherent sign pattern, so with function proportional to that share the plain base barely moves from ~45 %.
The top-1 singular direction per matrix carries only a few percent of the delta's energy along its sign pattern, so it acts like a ~0.03 dose and stays near plain base.
The bulk outside the top 64 directions keeps most of the energy (~70 %) and the coherent signs, so it acts like a ~0.7 dose; on the plain curve (443 at 0.5, 463 at 1) that is about 87-90 %.
